findings.title: Async legacy write derives from request context which is canceled after response
findings.body: The goroutine wraps the request ctx with a timeout. The apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the handler returns, which is immediately after the goroutine is spawned. The legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection calls will therefore often fail with context canceled, and legacy storage silently diverges. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the timeout. The same pattern appears at lines 110, 135 and 163.

findings.title: Storage failure recorded as legacy duration metric
findings.body: In Create, a failure from d.Storage.Create is recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration. Update has the same mistake at line 129. As a result, storage errors are attributed to the legacy store in metrics.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The asynchronous legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded with recordStorageDuration rather than recordLegacyDuration. This skews storage metrics and hides legacy failures.

findings.title: Delete metric uses name instead of kind label
findings.body: On success, Delete calls recordStorageDuration with `name` in the kind position. This produces a metric label per object name, which is a cardinality explosion, and the label value is wrong.

findings.title: Delete puts base logger in context, dropping fields
findings.body: Delete calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` with the base logger instead of `log`. The name, kind and method values built on the line above are therefore lost for downstream logging.

findings.title: Async legacy write errors are never logged
findings.body: Errors from the background legacy writes are only counted in metrics, never logged. The previous synchronous code logged legacy failures. Divergence between the stores is now invisible in logs.

findings.title: Legacy update reuses objInfo concurrently/after request
findings.body: objInfo is passed unchanged to the background legacy Update, while the old updateWrapper with the storage-updated object is no longer used. Patch-based objInfo is evaluated against the legacy object, so the legacy store may end up with different content than unified storage. The same objInfo is also used across goroutines after the request has finished.

findings.title: Create error case mocks legacy, not storage; async calls unasserted
findings.body: The case named "unified store fails" sets up the failure on the legacy mock via setupLegacyFn. The legacy and storage mocks share one mock instance, so the test passes by accident. None of the tests wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy calls.
